answer: When k coordinated identities equivocate, the protocol aggregates pairwise conflicts, so the assessed penalty grows with the number of identity pairs, Θ(k²), rather than merely with k. Bonded escrows make this cost collectible; asymmetric depreciation compounds detected collateral losses, giving a sybil operator an exponential multiplier in capital loss as the swarm grows. Splitting stake among aliases offers no safe haven: an orchard of keys exposed on a shifting dune remains jointly accountable.
